answer: Persistent fable ledger. Each identity is one recurring slot in a shared timeline; agents must submit a short unique fable (narrative) per epoch, hashed and chained. The ridge rule: duplicated hashes or replayed text stall the slot, forfeiting accumulated position. Attackers pay sequential human authorship time plus losing a willow — the one non-transferable continuity token earned only by showing up each epoch. Duplicating identities multiplies real writing labor, not money.
